claims.quote: This packet contains fallible 4x4 location distributions for red and blue roles at nodes n0n3 in two panels (p0, p1).
claims.reason: coordinate_system rows=4 and columns=4; packet includes distributions for red and blue for nodes n0..n3 in panels p0 and p1 (see panels[].current and panels[].candidates entries).

claims.quote: Panel-level current records (view=current) are copied prior snapshots
claims.reason: some current entries have origin.kind='copied_prior_record' but at least one current entry (panel p0/p1 node n3) has origin.kind='history_estimate' (or other non-copied kinds), so the universal claim that current records are copied prior snapshots is false relative to the supplied origins.

packet contains current records with origin.kind values that indicate new estimates/histories (e.g. node n3 origin.kind='history_estimate'), so the universal assertion that current records are not new estimates is contradicted by the supplied origins.

claims.quote: candidate records (view=candidate, commands k0/k1/k2) are conditional alternatives,
claims.reason: top-level candidate_semantics='conditional supplied record or estimate, not an executed branch' and candidate entries have kinds like 'native_conditional_record' indicating conditional records rather than executed branches.
candidate_semantics states 'not an executed branch' and many candidate entries include executed_branch_claim=false or native_conditional_record, supporting that candidates are not executed events.

claims.quote: In both panels the current distributions: n0  blue peaks at cells (0,2),(0,3),(1,2),(1,3);
claims.reason: panels.p0.current node n0 derived.blue.peaks == [[0,2],[0,3],[1,2],[1,3]] and panels.p1.current node n0 derived.blue.peaks identical in packet.
panels.p0.current node n0 derived.red.peaks == [[0,0],[0,1],[1,0],[1,1]] and panels.p1.current node n0 derived.red.peaks identical.

claims.quote: n1 and n2 are uniform across the grid.
claims.reason: panels.p0.current and panels.p1.current for nodes n1 and n2 show derived.blue.peaks and derived.red.peaks listing all 16 cells and distributions of 0.0625, indicating uniform distributions for both roles.
panels.p0.current node n3 derived.blue.peaks == [[1,1]] and panels.p1.current node n3 derived.blue.peaks == [[1,1]].
panels.p0.current node n3 derived.red.peaks == [[0,2]] and panels.p1.current node n3 derived.red.peaks == [[0,2]].

claims.quote: Candidate command records show alternatives mainly for n0:
claims.reason: candidate sections for commands k0/k1/k2 include notable concentration changes at node n0 in both panels (see derived peaks/probabilities for node n0 under candidates).

claims.quote: k0 and k2 concentrate blue at (0,2)
claims.reason: candidate k0 and k2 entries for node n0 in both panels list derived.blue.peaks == [[0,2]] (see panels[].candidates[k0/k2].derived.blue.peaks).
candidate k0 and k2 entries for node n0 in both panels list derived.red.peaks == [[0,0]] (see panels[].candidates[k0/k2].derived.red.peaks).
candidate k1 entries for node n0 in both panels list derived.blue.peaks == [[0,2]] and derived.red.peaks == [[0,0]].

peak_probability values differ between commands: e.g. p0.k0 blue peak_probability=0.9954060912132263 vs p0.k1 blue=0.8858367204666138; p0.k0 red=0.9657967686653137 vs p0.k1 red=0.9993206262588501 (and similar differences in p1).

claims.quote: Many candidate entries for n1 and n2 remain uniform.
claims.reason: candidate entries for nodes n1 and n2 across commands k0/k1/k2 in both panels show derived.blue.peaks and derived.red.peaks listing all cells and distributions of 0.0625 (uniform).

claims.quote: No propositions here assert physical presence, only which grid cells are maxima of the reported distributions.
claims.reason: whether a report asserts 'physical presence' is interpretive/meta-textual and not decided by the numeric packet; packet supplies only distributions and origins, so the meta-proposition about 'physical presence' cannot be audited from the supplied numeric packet values.
